headline_marked: MediaTek [[Dimensity 9600 Pro]] debuts with 2nm architecture, beating Qualcomm to the punch
headline: MediaTek Dimensity 9600 Pro debuts with 2nm architecture, beating Qualcomm to the punch
summary: MediaTek's new flagship chip boasts a 2nm process, advanced AI capabilities, and improved GPU performance, aiming to challenge Samsung and Qualcomm.
details: MediaTek has officially announced the Dimensity 9600 Pro processor, built on a cutting-edge 2nm architecture. This new chip is set to compete directly with Samsung's Exynos 2600 and aims to surpass Qualcomm's offerings in the mobile processor market.

The Dimensity 9600 Pro features a 2+3+3 core configuration with enhanced L2 and L3 cache, supporting the latest LPDDR6 memory and UFS 5 storage. Its 'Fusion Architecture' intelligently divides AI tasks between the CPU and NPU for faster on-device processing.

With a dual NPU design, including MediaTek's 10th generation Super Performance NPU and eNPU 2.0, the 9600 Pro offers a 51% performance boost and 40% better power efficiency compared to its predecessor.

While clock speeds are not disclosed, MediaTek claims a 17% increase in single-core and 15% in multi-core performance. The integrated GPU includes a third-generation ray-tracing engine, promising an 18% improvement in ray-traced gaming and native support for up to 185fps.
The new Image Signal Processor (ISP) supports 60fps action capture, 4K slow-motion video at 240fps, and 4K 120fps Cinematic LOG capture, leveraging the NPU for features like 4K Live Photo.

Additional features include AI-optimized cellular connectivity, AI-assisted satellite positioning, and Bluetooth 6.2 support. MediaTek has not yet revealed specific device partners or launch dates, but devices are expected by the end of 2026.
caption:

topic: 2028 volvo xc60 xc90 plug-in hybrid refresh
headline_marked: Volvo XC60 & XC90 [[plug-in hybrid range more than doubles]] to 78 miles
headline: Volvo XC60 & XC90 plug-in hybrid range more than doubles to 78 miles
summary: The refreshed SUVs boast new infotainment with Gemini AI and significantly larger batteries, offering up to 78 miles of electric driving.
details: Volvo has refreshed its popular XC60 and XC90 plug-in hybrid SUVs, with the most significant upgrade being a substantial increase in electric-only range. The XC60 T8 now features a 37.9 kWh battery, boosting its EPA-rated electric range to 78 miles, more than double the previous 35 miles. The larger XC90 T8 also receives the same battery upgrade, providing an electric range of 73 miles.

These updated models also incorporate Volvo's latest infotainment system, featuring an 11.2-inch screen powered by the Android Automotive OS. A key addition is the Gemini personal assistant, which offers conversational voice control for the infotainment system. Early testing suggests this new voice assistant performs notably better than its predecessor.

Beyond the powertrain and infotainment, the XC60 receives subtle exterior styling updates, including revised 'Thor's Hammer' headlights with matrix LED projectors and a slimmer front grille. New interior options include ventilated leather. Production for the XC60 will also expand to Volvo's plant in South Carolina, USA, to better serve the large North American market.

The XC90, while having undergone a more recent update, also benefits from the new infotainment system and the larger battery. Volvo states that the increased electric range is sufficient for three days of typical daily driving for the average US commuter, aiming to provide a clearer path to electrification for its customers.
caption:
